q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM( SELECT DISTINCT C.CUSTOMER_ID,COUNT(DISTINCT C.PRODUCT_KEY) FROM CUSTOMER C GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT C.PRODUCT_KEY)= ( SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT ) ) TEMP
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM( SELECT DISTINCT C.CUSTOMER_ID,COUNT(DISTINCT C.PRODUCT_KEY) FROM CUSTOMER C GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT C.PRODUCT_KEY)= ( SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT ) ) TEMP
explanation: Both queries aim to find customer IDs who have purchased all distinct products available in the system. They achieve this by comparing the count of distinct product keys purchased by each customer with the total count of distinct product keys in the PRODUCT table.
